correctness.rationale: Exact renewal-reward integrals yield the stated expressions for both clocks, including a=b. Defining B and g reduces the difference to a scaled difference of g at two rates. The elasticity r(x)=x*g_prime(x)/g(x) decreases strictly because J(x)=(x+2)exp(-x)-(2-x) has positive derivative, yielding a unique crossing for every a,b>0; the equal-rate limit is x*g_prime(x). Numeric and 8064 exact-rational tests confirm distinct formulae without replacing the infinite proof. Strict endpoints and stationary existence are explicit.

value.rationale: Transient suitability following disturbance but before senescence is a natural age window in successional ecology. Comparing disturbance regularity at identical average interval is a motivated environmental management contrast. This theorem gives complete rate-uniform sign classification and quantitative crossover bounds, rather than a finite slice, an observed numerical reversal or a standard renewal identity. It is a useful baseline but is not a field prescription or species extinction result.
